description_en: Named after its long, rectangular, (i.e.lāmco) shape, Lāma Pāṭī is located to the south of Patan Darbar Square. Due to its size and its 2,5-storey configuration, thepāṭīshould actually be classified as asataḥ,which means that "it is an integral part of the original endowment [of a temple complex, CB] that made funds available for the annual feasts" (Gutschow2011, 640). The 13-baypāṭīwas established by two ministers of King Srinivasa Malla in 1678 CE (NS 795) and used to house an Umamahesvara shrine. More than ten per cent of all arcaded resthouses are integrated into two-storeysataḥsin Patan (ibid.641). Thepāṭīwas constructed by order of the minister Bhagīratha Bhaiyā (also known as Bhāga Kājī). Not much is known about Bhagīratha's family background. The building is also known as Tāhāḥ Phale (lit. ‘apāṭīin rectangular shape’) amongst local residents.Kings and princes of various kingdoms such as Bhaktapur, Kantipur and Tanahun attended the inaugural ceremony of thepāṭī. Kings from twelve kingdoms were invited to this, as well as to the inaugural ceremony of Bhāidegaḥ (LAL1200) which was also built on Bhagīratha's orders. The kings were received at the bays of this Pāṭī (cp.VajrācāryaVS 2022, 28), which was built in a Malla style (seeOldfield, 1855:http://www.bl.ukfor the sketch of this Pāṭī).The inscription installed at thepāṭīinforms us that a statue of Umāmaheśvara was once housed there.Gutschow(2011, 641) states that the sanctum of the deity was located under the octagonal pinnacle. Local people argue that this statue is still kept on its ground floor. However, since all the bays of Pāṭī are currently occupied by shops it was not possible for us to approach and inspect the site. Thepāṭīcurrently has 13 bays, though Oldfield's sketch shows it with 10.Gutschow(2011, 642) writes that, "the variation of lotus foliage and the petals around the central square opening demonstrates the creativity of the cavers who were not bound by strict rules."Thepāṭīwas given its present shape after the earthquakes of VS 1910. The top storey and tower collapsed in the Great Earthquake of 1934 CE and were later modified to reflect a contemporary style. In 1994/95 GTZ/UDLE funded the reconstruction of the building. It was rebuilt with projecting windows and a pinnacle. Historical photographs and a watercolour sketch by Ambrose Oldfield (1855) provided helpful indications of the structure's original design. The watercolour was published in the Illustrated London News in 1855, constituting what was "probably one of the first published images from Nepal in the West" (Gutschow2011, 645).Today, the L-shaped Pāṭī is managed by the Department of Archaeology. The DoA rents out the ground floor to a variety of shops and the upper floor is used as a restaurant. Attempts by conservationists to reduce the amount of unsightly signage have so far been unsuccessful. The building is poorly maintained, and this has only become worse after the earthquake of 2015 struck. New construction work has been carried out in the back yard since 2018.
description_ne: पाटन दरबार क्षेत्रको दक्षिणमा यो पाटी अवस्थित छ । लाम्चो आकारमा बनेको पाटी भएबाट बनोटको आधारमा यसलाई ''लाम पाटी'' भनिएको हो । स्थानीयहरू यसलाई ''ताहाःफले'' (नेवारी) भन्ने गर्छन् जसको ठिक नेपाली अनुवाद ''लामो आकारको पाटी'' भन्ने नै हुन्छ । यसको निर्माण ने.सं. ७९५ मा मन्त्री भगीरथ भैयाले गरेका हुन् । उनलाई 'भाग काजी' पनि भनिन्थ्यो । भगीरथ भैयाको पारिवारिक पृष्ठभूमि स्पष्ट छैन । उनको नामको पछाडि रहेको 'भैया' शब्दको आधारमा उनलाई तराई मूलका मानी अड्कल गरिएको पनि पाइन्छ तर यस अनुमानलाई प्रमाणित गर्ने ठोस प्रमाण पाइएको छैन ।श्रीनिवास मल्लले "म र भगीरथ भैयामा कुनै फरक मैले देखेको छैन, अरुले पनि फरक सम्झनु हुँदैन" भन्ने उल्लेख गरेर शिलापत्रमा कुँदाएर ललितपुरको प्रसिद्ध त:बाहाल मन्दिरमा राख्न लगाएका थिए (Vajrācārya 2056, 173) । यो तथ्यबाट भगीरथ राजा श्रीनिवासले निकै विश्वासमा लिएका चौतरा (मन्त्री) थिए भन्ने सहजै अनुमान हुन्छ । श्रीनिवास मल्लपछि राजा भएका योगनरेन्द्र मल्लले भगीरथ भैयाप्रति ईर्ष्या गरी उनले रानीहरूप्रति शिष्ट व्यवहार नगरेको  आरोप लगाई नेसं ८०४ माघ शुक्ल ५ श्रीपञ्चमीको दिनमा चौतारा पदबाट बर्खास्त गरेका थिए (Regmi 1966, 96). भगीरथ भैयाले दाउपेच गरी षडयन्त्र गर्नसक्ने भयले योगनरेन्द्रले नेसं ८०५ भाद्र कृष्ण ३ मा भगीरथ भैयालाई  मार्न लगाए (Regmi 1966, 95).भगीरथले लाम पाटी निर्माण पश्चात राख्न लगाएको शिलापत्रमा उमामहेश्वरको मूर्ति पनि स्थापना गरिएको चर्चा छ । भूमि तल्लामा भएको फल्चामा उक्त उमामहेश्वरको मूर्ति रहेको कुरा स्थानीय बताउछन् । हाल भूमि तल्लका सबै कवलहरूमा पसल खोलिएबाट मूर्ति एवं शिलापत्र भए–नभएको जानकारी पाउन सकिएको छैन । यस पाटीको निर्माण भई  समापन समारोहमा पाटन लगायत भक्तपुराका र कान्तिपुरका राजा–राजकुमार एवं तनहुका भैया(?) रूद्रसेनको समेत उपस्थित भएका थिए । भगीरथले नै बनाएको भाइदेगः (LAL1200)को समापन समारोहमा पनि १२ देशका राजाहरू बोलइएका थिए । ती राजाहरूलाई यसै पाटीका १२ वटा कवलहरूमा राखी सत्कार गरिएको थियो (Vajrācārya 2022, 28).ओल्डफिल्डले बनाएको स्केचमा यस पाटी मल्लकालीन मौलिक स्वरूपमै भएको देखिन्छ (Oldfield, 1855:http://www.bl.uk) । उनको स्केचमा पाटी १० कवलको भएको देखिन्छ भने हाल १३ कवलको रहेको छ । वि.सं. १९९० को भूकम्पमा पाटीमाथिको पुर भत्किएपछि जस्तापाटाको प्रयोग गरी पुर आधुनिक स्वरूपमा बनाइएको थियो । पछि सन् १९९५ मा GTZ/udle को सहयोगमा पाटी  मौलिक स्वरूपमा पुनःनिर्माण गरिएको हो । हाल पाटीमा पसल र माथिल्लो तल्लामा रेष्टुरेन्ट राखिएबाट पाटीको शोभा घटेको देखिन्छ ।

historical_events.event_description: The monument was constructed in 1675 by two ministers of King Śrīnivāsa Malla. One was Bhagīratha Bhaiyāer (cautārā). The kings and princesses of Lalitpur, Kantipur and Bhaktapur including Bhaiyā(?) Rudrasena of Tanahu attended the inauguration ceremony of the Pāṭī.AYajñaritual was also performed at the same time. A person named Rājavãśa Rāvatta Narasiṁha is mentioned as the caretaker (chintāyāka) of the construction work.The inscription established in Taḥ Bahāḥ by order of King Śrīnivāsa Malla gives us a hint that the King placed great trust in Bhagīratha. Part of the inscription reads: “I see no difference between me and Bhagīratha Bhaiyā, [therefore] others also should not see any difference between him and me” (seeVajrācāryaVS 2056, 173 for the inscription). King Yoganarendra Malla, who succeeded Śrīnivāsa, accused Bhagīratha of mistreating the former’s queens and dismissed him from his post on the 5th bright fortnight of Māgha in NS 804 (seeRegmi1966, appendix III, p. 96). Bhagīratha Bhaiyā was killed by order of Yoganarendra on the 3rd dark fortnight of Bhādra in NS 805 (Regmi1966, appendix III, p. 95).
The pagoda style tower (pura) collapsed in the Great Earthquake of 1934 CE. The arcade survived (Gutschow 2011, 641). A few months later, the tower was replaced in a contemporary style.
In the 1980s CE, the upper floor of the monument was used as a police station. Afterwards, the Pāṭī became known as "Thanāpāṭī" (police-station pāṭī).

The Pāṭī was dismantled in 1994 and rebuilt with projecting windows and a pinnacle. The work was finished in 1995 with financial support from GTZ/UDLE.Gutschow(2011) reports that the upper storey with its projecting windows and the pinnacle were (re)constructed in 1995 with Henry Ambrose Oldfield's watercolour of 1855 used as a blueprint.
